posts.text:
The last question I ask every SDR candidate has nothing to do with sales.

"What do you think this job actually is?"

Most people answer with the activity. Making calls. Hitting quota. Booking meetings.

Correct, and completely useless to me.

The ones I hire answer with a person.

They say something about the guy on the other end of the phone who's mid-shift, three problems deep, and did not ask to be interrupted.

That answer tells me they've already imagined the human before they've imagined the pitch.

Everyone can describe the activity.

I'm listening for who they think is picking up.

Understanding their world and what we can do for them.

My top SDR says nothing for 4 seconds after a prospect finishes talking.

I timed it. On purpose. Because I thought she was freezing up.

She wasn't. She was waiting.

Here's what happens in those 4 seconds: → The prospect adds the part they were holding back → You get the real problem, not the polite version → You stop sounding like a survey

Every new rep fills silence because silence feels like failure. It makes them nervous and they start yapping and product feature dumping… lord.. what we told them NOT to do.

The best tool on a cold call is not the dialer.. it’s the silence.. the most persuasive tool on the call.

Remember Say less to Get more.

I almost gave one of my 15 reps a warning she didn't deserve last week.

Her EOD report wasn't in. Second time this week.

So I told Viktor: "If her EOD isn't in by 9:30pm, send a second warning and add me to the DM. First time is a mistake. Twice is a pattern."
9:31pm, Viktor replies.

"Update: she actually DID submit. 177 calls, 58 connects, 2 appointments booked. Posted at 7:28pm."

She just copy pasted yesterday's template and forgot to change the date in the header. The numbers were clearly today's.

"No second warning needed. Worth a quick nudge about labeling, but not the accountability issue you were worried about."

Read that again.

Viktor stopped me from having the wrong conversation with a rep who did everything right.

Leading 15 SDRs means you're always one bad assumption away from losing trust. The reps don't remember the 100 times you got it right. They remember the one time you accused them of something they didn't do.
Accountability without accuracy is just ego.

Hire viktor.com for your team. $100 in credits included, no card. Full link in first comment.

"Just send me an email."

My reps are not allowed to say yes to that.

Because that sentence means "I would like off this phone politely," and most SDRs hear it as a win.

Here's what my team says instead:

"Happy to. So I don't send you something useless, what's the one thing that would make it worth opening?"

Three things happen: 
→ You get a real answer, or you get the truth that there isn't one 
→ Your email now has a subject line the prospect wrote for you
 → The call keeps going

An email is not a win.

It's a hang-up with better manners.

Ask what goes in it.
